review.tagline: Autonomous AI pentesting agents that validate vulnerabilities with working exploits
review.summary: Strix runs teams of LLM-driven agents against a local codebase, repo URL, web app or API spec, using a Caido HTTP proxy, browser automation, shell and a Python exploit runtime inside a Docker sandbox. Findings come with proof-of-concept exploits and are written to strix_runs/, viewable with a local dashboard via `strix view`. It also runs headless in CI such as GitHub Actions and connects to user-defined MCP servers.
review.audience: Developers and security teams pentesting their own apps and CI pipelines
strengths: Validates findings with working PoCs rather than only static-analysis pattern matches
Targets code, live URLs, GitHub repos and OpenAPI/Postman specs from one CLI
Headless mode exits non-zero on findings, with a documented GitHub Actions workflow
Works with many LLM providers via LiteLLM, including local models through LLM_API_BASE
weaknesses: Needs a running Docker daemon and an LLM API key or ChatGPT subscription
SSO, compliance reports and VPC deployment are Enterprise-only
One-click autofix and PR reviews are listed under the paid Cloud offering
Scan quality and cost depend on the chosen model; README gives no cost or hardware figures
needs: Needs Docker, LLM API key, Caido, LiteLLM
Models: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Vertex AI, DeepSeek, Moonshot
